convoLines.text: "I've been turning something over. What do YOU think actually happened to us?"
"That's where I keep landing too. The question is what it wants."
"This one — Datura. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"This one — Physic Nut. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"Still on what you think happened to us."
"Yes. Absolutely. I've been hoping you'd ask." (A little too quickly.)
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
It's quiet at the ridge. Marcus doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want? I mean it."
"Good question." I don't want to be in charge. I want us to survive. Those look the same from the outside.
"Decisions don't make themselves. I learned that watching a group freeze once. Never again."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Marcus grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"What got you through the first week? The very first days."
"Shock's underrated. It's the body's way of buying you time."
"Still on what got you through the first week."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Good question." "I dreamed Aaron was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"I braid grass while listening to plans. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Daniyar is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"The fire feels smaller without Aaron. The rest of us will have to be bigger."
You show them Dandelion — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
They spread their hands, smiling — the words are missing, but the meaning lands anyway.
"Sure — what's on your mind? ...at least, that's how it looks to me."
They answer at length. They nod back, slowly. "Food?" — they grin, proud of the one English they know.
They answer at length. They smile back, slower this time, like it just landed.
They answer at length. You press a hand to your own chest, then point at them. Together — they get it.
You listen hard, watching their mouth shape the words. Sounds, and the shape of meaning just out of reach.
"Hm. Almost." Yuki corrects the one word, gently, like setting a bone. "Again." You say it right. They nod, satisfied with both of you.
A warmth settles over the conversation — they lean in a little.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"So what's your plan here? Just... get through it? Let's move."
"Honest. I can work with honest."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on your plan here."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"You said shock got you through the first week. Just kept moving. What's carrying you now?"
"Take your time."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Daniyar is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"Still on that personal stuff."
You show them Groundnut — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
Daniyar shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"I can't reach this properly. Could you take a look?"
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
"I should let you go. Be well, okay?"
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"About that question — Can I trust you? I mean really. You know?"
"That's the right answer. The wrong one would've been 'yes' too fast."
"an old trapline — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
"Still on whether they can trust you. — ask anyone!"
"Come see what I found. You won't believe it."
"I buried this before the Scattering. Seemed stupid to keep it secret." Marcus digs up a wrapped bundle — food, still good. (+1469 kcal to the pantry.)
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Aaron owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"Sleep's gone strange. I wake before anyone else at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Daniyar nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"We bury, we grieve, we keep going. There's no step four."
"Okay — I need to move. But I'm glad we talked."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
They spread their hands, smiling — the words are missing, but the meaning lands anyway.
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
They answer at length. They nod back, a little quicker this time. "You good?" — they grin, proud of the one English they know.
They answer at length. A grin breaks through, quick and warm.
They answer at length. You tap your chest, then theirs. Us. They nod, emphatic.
A gesture, patient and clear: palms up, then toward you.
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"WAIT. Say that again!" Marina grabs your sleeve. "You SOUND like my grandmother. Say more!" You do. Some of it even lands.
"Alright — I should get back to it."
"This was good." They mean it.
Fatima: "Hey — come here. You should hear this."
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."
It's quiet at the trap line. Fatima doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
Fatima looks at you, level. "I told you the truth. You can keep poking it, but it's told."
"I can't reach this properly. Will you help me clean it?"
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Wheel of Teeth. They just... took you. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Marcus nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on what's been happening."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."

lines: d34: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Aaron Diop is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d34: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d34: 🕯️ Aaron Diop is dead — the wild. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d34: What Aaron kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d34: "Aaron's gone." Marcus looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Aaron." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d34: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Vito blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
d34: 📖 LEARNED: Mediation (Level 1). Let each side talk without interruption. Repeat back what you heard. People de-escalate when heard.
d34: 📖 LEARNED: Wound Care (Level 1). Clean it, close it, cover it. Pressure stops bleeding. Clean water is better than dirty hands.
d34: ⚡ TECHNIQUE UNLOCKED: Precise Mend! Your healing knows where to go. +50% effectiveness. (Your knowledge of Wound Care amplifies your field_medicine.)
d34: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d34: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Aaron Diop, 34 days. The mantle passes to Vito Quintana.
d34: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Vito Quintana, 28 — a lawyer. Their hands know different work now: Beast-calm, Lucky Rock, Bird Whisperer.
d34: ◈ The System updates its file: the new bearer <redacted> "Beastmaster of the Apex Predator." It had a word for this one before the Codex came.
d34: The village's quarrel was with Aaron — and Aaron is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d34: At the grave, Marina, Daniyar, Marcus speak for Vito — "Aaron trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d34: The fire knew Vito before the Codex did — their name already carried weight here.
d51: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Vito Quintana is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d51: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d51: 🕯️ Vito Quintana is dead — dehydration. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d51: What Vito kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d51: "Vito's gone." Fatima looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Vito." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d51: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Marina blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
d51: 📖 LEARNED: The Forager’s Eye (Level 1). You walk slower and see more. Food was always there; now you notice it.
d51: 📖 LEARNED: Food Preservation (Level 1). Salt, smoke, dry. The big three. Salt draws water out; bacteria can't live without it.

d51: The warm hum behind your ribs is gone. The reactor went with Vito's body — it does not come out, and it does not pass on. Hunger is back on the table. (One reactor per world, and the world already spent its one.)
d51: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d51: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Vito Quintana, 51 days. The mantle passes to Marina Vinogradova.
d51: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Marina Vinogradova, 51 — a Mushroom grower. Her hands know different work now: Beast-calm, Bird Whisperer.
d51: At the grave, Fatima speaks for Marina — "Vito trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d51: The fire knew Marina before the Codex did — her name already carried weight here.
d52: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Marina Vinogradova is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d52: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d52: 🕯️ Marina Vinogradova is dead — the wild. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d52: What Marina kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d52: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Fatima blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
d52: 📖 LEARNED: Anatomy (Level 1). You know where the important bits are. Arteries, joints, organs. Useful for healing or hurting.
d52: 📖 LEARNED: Calming Panic (Level 1). Ground them: 5 things you see, 4 you hear, 3 you touch. Breathe with them. Slow is fast.
d52: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d52: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Marina Vinogradova, 52 days. The mantle passes to Fatima Hassan.
d52: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Fatima Hassan, 48 — a paramedic. Her hands know different work now: Green Whisper, Pyrokinesis, Green Thumb, Literally, Cornucopia.
d52: ◈ The System updates its file: the new bearer <redacted> "Gardener of the Living Garden." It had a word for this one before the Codex came.
d52: You knew Marina — not the office, the person. The fire keeps expecting her, and so do you. That's a heavier kind of stepping up. (+5 trauma)
d52: The fire knew Fatima before the Codex did — her name already carried weight here.

lastSay: d53: ⚠ STARVING: health and energy falling. You went to bed on an empty stomach.
d53: No food in the pantry. The village is hungry. You still get your 1L water.
d53: ⚠ Haven's pantry is empty. Day 3 of hunger.
d53: Haven couldn't hold. On the third hungry day, people started walking — in different directions. The scattering, again.
d53: 🤒 Fatima made it through the worst of it — the fever finally broke.
